chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar from Abdullah ibn al-Munbih from al-Husayn ibn 'Alwan from 'Amr ibn Khalid from Zayd ibn 'Ali from his father from his forefathers from Ali (peace be upon him): That a man came to him and said,

O Commander of the Faithful, by God, I love you for God's sake. He said to him, 'But I hate you for God's sake.' He said, 'And why?' He said, 'Because you seek profit in the Adhan and you take a wage for teaching the Quran. And I heard the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) saying, 'Whoever takes a wage for teaching the Quran, his share on the Day of Resurrection [will be]...''
ai.seo_question: Why did Imam Ali hate a man he loved for God's sake?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the Shia scholarly distinction between *Ibadah* (worship) and *Kasb* (commerce), specifically critiquing the commodification of religious services like the Adhan and Quranic instruction. Imam Ali (AS) identifies the man's flaw not in his love, but in his transactional approach to sacred duties, linking this practice to the Prophet’s warning that such individuals forfeit their spiritual reward in favor of worldly gain. This underscores the principle that teaching the Quran should be an act of devotion rather than a commercial enterprise.
